newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Briton who caught AIDS says she was "naive".
newsitem.headline: Briton who caught AIDS says she was "naive".

text.p: A British woman who is accusing her former Cypriot lover of giving her the deadly AIDS virus described herself as "naive" in court on Thursday for trusting him.
In a charged atmosphere, 45-year-old Janette Pink told a court in Larnaca that she continued her affair with Pavlos Georgiou even after discovering she had caught AIDS from him.
"I loved him," she said quietly, picking nervously at a handkerchief she was holding. "It made sense for us to stay together because we had the same virus. I loved him - maybe I was naive."
Ten feet away ex-lover Georgiou, 40, sat in the dock. It was the couple's first encounter since Pink left the holiday island last June, when she was seriously ill.
Earlier in the day the judge ordered Georgiou arrested and brought to court after his lawyer said he was in hospital, too ill to appear. He is HIV positive.

Pink, who had an affair with father-of-four Georgiou from January 1994 until the summer of 1996, has accused him of giving her the virus and lying to her about the condition of his wife, who died of AIDS in 1994.
Looking painfully thin in a black and white floral print dress, Pink admitted it never entered her mind during the initial stages of their relationship to use any form of contraceptive.

"We weren't two youngsters having lots of affairs. I thought it would be safe to have sex with him. I never thought of the consequences, I just entered a normal relationship. It didn't even enter my head to use a condom," she said.
After several tests sparked by persistent rumours on Georgiou's condition, Pink tested positive for the HIV virus which causes AIDS in October 1994.
"I told him I knew he was HIV positive. I asked him why he didn't tell me. He didn't have any answer, he didn't apologise to me," said Pink.
Last year Pink had an abortion when doctors told her carrying a baby to full term would risk her health and that of the unborn child.
Georgiou has denied charges of negligently infecting Pink, from Basildon, Essex.
Earlier on Thursday Georgiou, was admitted to hospital complaining of a temperature, stomach cramps and vomiting.
He appeared better later as he walked unassisted to the courthouse, escorted by police, smiling broadly and giving a thumbs-up sign to cameras.

But his mood quickly changed in the packed courtroom as he sat grim-faced and hunched in his chair in the dock. Both he and Pink studiously avoided any eye contact, although Pink occasionally glanced in his direction.
Georgiou allowed himself a wry smile and shook his head slightly as Pink described the final stages of their relationship:
"I began to see a different side, a very aggressive side which frightened me," she said.
"As I got sick the knowledge of what Pavlos did to me suddenly hit me and I thought something should be done about it," she said.
Pink, accompanied by her parents and a relative, appeared slightly unsteady on her feet and was at times supported by her father, Vic Ruston.

Cypriot authorities are charging Georgiou for contravening a decades-old law banning the transmission of contagious diseases either unlawfully or negligently. The charge carries a penalty of up to two years in jail, a 1,500 pounds ($3,000) fine, or both.
